interventions.expected_effect: slope 14.5 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 4154.0-6121.0 m3/ha/yr (central 5116.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 2.1 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 5.9 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.6 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 3845.0-5794.0 m3/ha/yr (central 4760.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.3 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 3.7 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.72 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

residual_risks: groundwater depletion: fossil/non-renewable aquifer abstraction (aquifer yield and licence not assessed)
secondary salinisation/sodification if leaching or drainage fails
residual root-zone salinity above 4 dS/m limits sensitive crops
wind erosion/dust and flash-flood erosion are not modelled
soil depth and SOC come from third-party maps with no local validation (SoilGrids deserts: low skill for SOC)

residual_risks: groundwater depletion: fossil/non-renewable aquifer abstraction (aquifer yield and licence not assessed)
secondary salinisation/sodification if leaching or drainage fails
residual root-zone salinity above 4 dS/m limits sensitive crops
wind erosion/dust and flash-flood erosion are not modelled
soil depth and SOC come from third-party maps with no local validation (SoilGrids deserts: low skill for SOC)

scenarios.name: Treated-wastewater drip irrigation, salt-tolerant crops, leaching and gypsum
infrastructure: connection to a wastewater treatment plant outlet (distance NOT mapped)
residual_risks: treated-wastewater availability, distance to treatment plant and crop-use restrictions not assessed; salt and sodium load of effluent
secondary salinisation/sodification if leaching or drainage fails
residual root-zone salinity above 4 dS/m limits sensitive crops
wind erosion/dust and flash-flood erosion are not modelled
soil depth and SOC come from third-party maps with no local validation (SoilGrids deserts: low skill for SOC)

uncertainty.basis: SoilGrids 2.0 vs WoSIS measured, arid held-out sites (RMSE)
SoilGrids vs WoSIS arid RMSE; low skill in deserts
assumed; no local validation

observed: slope and elevation (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM)
climate normals and interannual rainfall (TerraClimate 2011-2020, gridded climate product)
crop/ESP/salinity tolerance tables are literature (see expert_rule)
ml_predicted: ECe and ESP (own LightGBM trained on measured WoSIS/Hassani points, conformal intervals)
pH, SOC, texture, coarse fragments, bulk density, CEC (SoilGrids 2.0, third party)
depth to bedrock (SoilGrids 2017, third party, capped 200 cm)
expert_rule: Maas-Hoffman salinity response (FAO IDP29 Table 4), ESP tolerance classes (FAO SB39), pH/SOC/coarse-fragment/texture/depth/slope response curves (assumed shapes)
relative erosion index (RUSLE-type structure)
FAO suitability class boundaries on relative yield (S1>=0.8, S2 0.6-0.8, S3 0.4-0.6 [assumed], N<0.4)
simulated: intervention outcomes (leaching, gypsum, organic amendment, terracing, water harvesting)
post-restoration relative yield, class and water requirement
feasibility score and interval (Monte-Carlo)

data_sources: WoSIS 2023-12 snapshot (ISRIC; CC BY / public-domain subset) - ECe training labels
Hassani et al. 2020 (Mendeley Data, CC BY 4.0) - ECe/ESP training points
SoilGrids 2.0 (ISRIC, CC BY 4.0) - pH, SOC, texture, CF, BD, CEC
SoilGrids 2017 BDRICM (ISRIC) - depth to bedrock
WorldClim 2.1 bioclim + elevation (CC BY 4.0) - ECe/ESP covariates
TerraClimate 2011-2020 (Abatzoglou et al. 2018) - rainfall, ET0
Copernicus GLO-30 DEM - slope
geoBoundaries gbOpen JOR ADM1 (CC BY 2.5) - boundary

limiting_factors.detail: annual rainfall 221.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 184.0 mm) vs barley season ET 520.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 32.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply
mean slope 8.5 deg (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, 50 m slope aggregated to 250 m)
relative water-erosion index 0.3 (RUSLE-type structure, not a soil-loss prediction; wind/flash-flood erosion not modelled)
coarse fragments about 26.0 vol %

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)
feasibility_meta.score_definition: probability, over input-uncertainty x parameter draws, that at least one evaluated scenario brings the best crop to relative yield >= 0.6 (FAO class S2 or better) under a reference water allocation of 8000 m3/ha/yr per unit (a scenario condition, not an observation)

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion
interventions.description: Converts slopes up to a practical limit (assumed 20-30 deg, soil depth >= 40 cm) into cultivable benches and reduces water erosion; abandonment/poor maintenance is the main failure mode.
interventions.expected_effect: slope 8.5 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 3678.0-5497.0 m3/ha/yr (central 4564.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.6 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 3.2 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.63 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

SoilGrids 2.0 (ISRIC, CC BY 4.0) - pH, SOC, texture, CF, BD, CEC
SoilGrids 2017 BDRICM (ISRIC) - depth to bedrock
WorldClim 2.1 bioclim + elevation (CC BY 4.0) - ECe/ESP covariates
TerraClimate 2011-2020 (Abatzoglou et al. 2018) - rainfall, ET0
Copernicus GLO-30 DEM - slope
geoBoundaries gbOpen JOR ADM1 (CC BY 2.5) - boundary

limiting_factors.detail: annual rainfall 203.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 156.0 mm) vs barley season ET 522.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 27.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply
mean slope 12.6 deg (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, 50 m slope aggregated to 250 m)
relative water-erosion index 0.42 (RUSLE-type structure, not a soil-loss prediction; wind/flash-flood erosion not modelled)
coarse fragments about 34.0 vol %

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)
feasibility_meta.score_definition: probability, over input-uncertainty x parameter draws, that at least one evaluated scenario brings the best crop to relative yield >= 0.6 (FAO class S2 or better) under a reference water allocation of 8000 m3/ha/yr per unit (a scenario condition, not an observation)

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion
interventions.description: Converts slopes up to a practical limit (assumed 20-30 deg, soil depth >= 40 cm) into cultivable benches and reduces water erosion; abandonment/poor maintenance is the main failure mode.
interventions.expected_effect: slope 12.6 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 3775.0-5664.0 m3/ha/yr (central 4680.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.3 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 3.8 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.82 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.5 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed

interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 4.8 % <= 5 % target)

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.68 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range. interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.58 %; improves water holding and infiltration

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: reduce ECe 5.9 -> 7.3 dS/m (simulated); reclamation leaching depth 0.0 m water per m soil = 0.0 m3/ha one-off (C/C0 = exp(-k r), k 1.6-2.3, FAO IDP29 80-90% removal at r=1)

interventions.expected_effect: reduce ECe 4.7 -> 4.1 dS/m (simulated); reclamation leaching depth 0.04 m water per m soil = 246.0 m3/ha one-off (C/C0 = exp(-k r), k 1.6-2.3, FAO IDP29 80-90% removal at r=1)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: 0.8 t/ha gypsum (0.3 m, effectiveness 0.5-0.9 assumed) lowers ESP 7.7 -> 5.0 %
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.51 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Salt/sodicity-tolerant crop selection (date palm, barley, tall wheatgrass, olive)
interventions.description: Choose crops whose Maas-Hoffman threshold exceeds the achievable root-zone ECe (FAO Table 4) and whose ESP class tolerates the residual sodicity.
interventions.expected_effect: crop choice keeps relative yield >= 0.6 at ECe 7.4 dS/m (post-reclamation, simulated)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

residual_risks: groundwater depletion: fossil/non-renewable aquifer abstraction (aquifer yield and licence not assessed)
secondary salinisation/sodification if leaching or drainage fails
residual root-zone salinity above 4 dS/m limits sensitive crops

post-restoration relative yield, class and water requirement

limiting_factors.detail: annual rainfall 26.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 25.0 mm) vs barley season ET 673.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 3.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)
feasibility_meta.score_definition: probability, over input-uncertainty x parameter draws, that at least one evaluated scenario brings the best crop to relative yield >= 0.6 (FAO class S2 or better) under a reference water allocation of 8000 m3/ha/yr per unit (a scenario condition, not an observation)

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion
interventions.description: Converts slopes up to a practical limit (assumed 20-30 deg, soil depth >= 40 cm) into cultivable benches and reduces water erosion; abandonment/poor maintenance is the main failure mode.
interventions.expected_effect: slope 0.3 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 6679.0-9004.0 m3/ha/yr (central 7695.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency

interventions.expected_effect: reduce ECe 5.3 -> 7.4 dS/m (simulated); reclamation leaching depth 0.0 m water per m soil = 0.0 m3/ha one-off (C/C0 = exp(-k r), k 1.6-2.3, FAO IDP29 80-90% removal at r=1)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: 3.5 t/ha gypsum (0.3 m, effectiveness 0.5-0.9 assumed) lowers ESP 9.4 -> 5.0 %
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.6 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Salt/sodicity-tolerant crop selection (date palm, barley, tall wheatgrass, olive)
interventions.description: Choose crops whose Maas-Hoffman threshold exceeds the achievable root-zone ECe (FAO Table 4) and whose ESP class tolerates the residual sodicity.
interventions.expected_effect: crop choice keeps relative yield >= 0.6 at ECe 7.4 dS/m (post-reclamation, simulated)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

scenarios.name: Treated-wastewater drip irrigation, salt-tolerant crops, leaching and gypsum
infrastructure: connection to a wastewater treatment plant outlet (distance NOT mapped)
residual_risks: treated-wastewater availability, distance to treatment plant and crop-use restrictions not assessed; salt and sodium load of effluent
secondary salinisation/sodification if leaching or drainage fails
residual root-zone salinity above 4 dS/m limits sensitive crops
wind erosion/dust and flash-flood erosion are not modelled
soil depth and SOC come from third-party maps with no local validation (SoilGrids deserts: low skill for SOC)

residual root-zone salinity above 4 dS/m limits sensitive crops
wind erosion/dust and flash-flood erosion are not modelled
soil depth and SOC come from third-party maps with no local validation (SoilGrids deserts: low skill for SOC)

observed: slope and elevation (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM)
climate normals and interannual rainfall (TerraClimate 2011-2020, gridded climate product)

ml_predicted: ECe and ESP (own LightGBM trained on measured WoSIS/Hassani points, conformal intervals)
pH, SOC, texture, coarse fragments, bulk density, CEC (SoilGrids 2.0, third party)
depth to bedrock (SoilGrids 2017, third party, capped 200 cm)

simulated: intervention outcomes (leaching, gypsum, organic amendment, terracing, water harvesting)
post-restoration relative yield, class and water requirement
feasibility score and interval (Monte-Carlo)

limiting_factors.detail: annual rainfall 17.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 16.0 mm) vs barley season ET 693.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 1.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)
feasibility_meta.score_definition: probability, over input-uncertainty x parameter draws, that at least one evaluated scenario brings the best crop to relative yield >= 0.6 (FAO class S2 or better) under a reference water allocation of 8000 m3/ha/yr per unit (a scenario condition, not an observation)

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion
interventions.description: Converts slopes up to a practical limit (assumed 20-30 deg, soil depth >= 40 cm) into cultivable benches and reduces water erosion; abandonment/poor maintenance is the main failure mode.
interventions.expected_effect: slope 0.7 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 6951.0-9258.0 m3/ha/yr (central 8032.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency

interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 5040.0-7186.0 m3/ha/yr (central 6132.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 3.5 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: 1.5 t/ha gypsum (0.3 m, effectiveness 0.5-0.9 assumed) lowers ESP 7.2 -> 5.0 %
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.4 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.expected_effect: 1.2 t/ha gypsum (0.3 m, effectiveness 0.5-0.9 assumed) lowers ESP 9.3 -> 5.0 %
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.4 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

residual_risks: groundwater depletion: fossil/non-renewable aquifer abstraction (aquifer yield and licence not assessed)
secondary salinisation/sodification if leaching or drainage fails
residual root-zone salinity above 4 dS/m limits sensitive crops

assumed; no local validation

limiting_factors.detail: annual rainfall 95.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 88.0 mm) vs barley season ET 593.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 12.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)
feasibility_meta.score_definition: probability, over input-uncertainty x parameter draws, that at least one evaluated scenario brings the best crop to relative yield >= 0.6 (FAO class S2 or better) under a reference water allocation of 8000 m3/ha/yr per unit (a scenario condition, not an observation)

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion
interventions.description: Converts slopes up to a practical limit (assumed 20-30 deg, soil depth >= 40 cm) into cultivable benches and reduces water erosion; abandonment/poor maintenance is the main failure mode.
interventions.expected_effect: slope 12.7 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 5477.0-7861.0 m3/ha/yr (central 6584.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: reduce ECe 7.0 -> 4.0 dS/m (simulated); reclamation leaching depth 0.19 m water per m soil = 1114.0 m3/ha one-off (C/C0 = exp(-k r), k 1.6-2.3, FAO IDP29 80-90% removal at r=1)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion
interventions.description: Converts slopes up to a practical limit (assumed 20-30 deg, soil depth >= 40 cm) into cultivable benches and reduces water erosion; abandonment/poor maintenance is the main failure mode.
interventions.expected_effect: slope 12.1 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 5499.0-8178.0 m3/ha/yr (central 6721.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: reduce ECe 7.4 -> 4.1 dS/m (simulated); reclamation leaching depth 0.0 m water per m soil = 0.0 m3/ha one-off (C/C0 = exp(-k r), k 1.6-2.3, FAO IDP29 80-90% removal at r=1)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: 2.7 t/ha gypsum (0.3 m, effectiveness 0.5-0.9 assumed) lowers ESP 10.7 -> 5.0 %
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.41 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

scenarios.name: Bench terraces with soil conservation and drip irrigation (sloping land)
residual_risks: groundwater depletion: fossil/non-renewable aquifer abstraction (aquifer yield and licence not assessed)
secondary salinisation/sodification if leaching or drainage fails
residual root-zone salinity above 4 dS/m limits sensitive crops
wind erosion/dust and flash-flood erosion are not modelled
soil depth and SOC come from third-party maps with no local validation (SoilGrids deserts: low skill for SOC)

uncertainty.basis: SoilGrids 2.0 vs WoSIS measured, arid held-out sites (RMSE)
SoilGrids vs WoSIS arid RMSE; low skill in deserts
assumed; no local validation

observed: slope and elevation (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM)
climate normals and interannual rainfall (TerraClimate 2011-2020, gridded climate product)
crop/ESP/salinity tolerance tables are literature (see expert_rule)
ml_predicted: ECe and ESP (own LightGBM trained on measured WoSIS/Hassani points, conformal intervals)
pH, SOC, texture, coarse fragments, bulk density, CEC (SoilGrids 2.0, third party)
depth to bedrock (SoilGrids 2017, third party, capped 200 cm)
expert_rule: Maas-Hoffman salinity response (FAO IDP29 Table 4), ESP tolerance classes (FAO SB39), pH/SOC/coarse-fragment/texture/depth/slope response curves (assumed shapes)
relative erosion index (RUSLE-type structure)
FAO suitability class boundaries on relative yield (S1>=0.8, S2 0.6-0.8, S3 0.4-0.6 [assumed], N<0.4)
simulated: intervention outcomes (leaching, gypsum, organic amendment, terracing, water harvesting)
post-restoration relative yield, class and water requirement
feasibility score and interval (Monte-Carlo)

data_sources: WoSIS 2023-12 snapshot (ISRIC; CC BY / public-domain subset) - ECe training labels
Hassani et al. 2020 (Mendeley Data, CC BY 4.0) - ECe/ESP training points
SoilGrids 2.0 (ISRIC, CC BY 4.0) - pH, SOC, texture, CF, BD, CEC

limiting_factors.detail: annual rainfall 233.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 194.0 mm) vs barley season ET 519.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 34.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply
mean slope 11.7 deg (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, 50 m slope aggregated to 250 m)
relative water-erosion index 0.47 (RUSLE-type structure, not a soil-loss prediction; wind/flash-flood erosion not modelled)
coarse fragments about 24.0 vol %

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)
feasibility_meta.score_definition: probability, over input-uncertainty x parameter draws, that at least one evaluated scenario brings the best crop to relative yield >= 0.6 (FAO class S2 or better) under a reference water allocation of 8000 m3/ha/yr per unit (a scenario condition, not an observation)

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion
interventions.description: Converts slopes up to a practical limit (assumed 20-30 deg, soil depth >= 40 cm) into cultivable benches and reduces water erosion; abandonment/poor maintenance is the main failure mode.
interventions.expected_effect: slope 11.7 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 3621.0-5456.0 m3/ha/yr (central 4501.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.6 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 4.1 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.77 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 3878.0-5827.0 m3/ha/yr (central 4944.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 2.2 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 5.6 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.57 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

secondary salinisation/sodification if leaching or drainage fails
wind erosion/dust and flash-flood erosion are not modelled
soil depth and SOC come from third-party maps with no local validation (SoilGrids deserts: low skill for SOC)

uncertainty.basis: SoilGrids 2.0 vs WoSIS measured, arid held-out sites (RMSE)
SoilGrids vs WoSIS arid RMSE; low skill in deserts
assumed; no local validation

observed: slope and elevation (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM)
climate normals and interannual rainfall (TerraClimate 2011-2020, gridded climate product)
crop/ESP/salinity tolerance tables are literature (see expert_rule)
ml_predicted: ECe and ESP (own LightGBM trained on measured WoSIS/Hassani points, conformal intervals)
pH, SOC, texture, coarse fragments, bulk density, CEC (SoilGrids 2.0, third party)
depth to bedrock (SoilGrids 2017, third party, capped 200 cm)
expert_rule: Maas-Hoffman salinity response (FAO IDP29 Table 4), ESP tolerance classes (FAO SB39), pH/SOC/coarse-fragment/texture/depth/slope response curves (assumed shapes)
relative erosion index (RUSLE-type structure)
FAO suitability class boundaries on relative yield (S1>=0.8, S2 0.6-0.8, S3 0.4-0.6 [assumed], N<0.4)
simulated: intervention outcomes (leaching, gypsum, organic amendment, terracing, water harvesting)
post-restoration relative yield, class and water requirement
feasibility score and interval (Monte-Carlo)

data_sources: WoSIS 2023-12 snapshot (ISRIC; CC BY / public-domain subset) - ECe training labels
Hassani et al. 2020 (Mendeley Data, CC BY 4.0) - ECe/ESP training points
SoilGrids 2.0 (ISRIC, CC BY 4.0) - pH, SOC, texture, CF, BD, CEC
SoilGrids 2017 BDRICM (ISRIC) - depth to bedrock
WorldClim 2.1 bioclim + elevation (CC BY 4.0) - ECe/ESP covariates
TerraClimate 2011-2020 (Abatzoglou et al. 2018) - rainfall, ET0
Copernicus GLO-30 DEM - slope
geoBoundaries gbOpen JOR ADM1 (CC BY 2.5) - boundary

limiting_factors.detail: Model 1 class 5: legal/environmental restriction. Restoration potential is not assessed; the restriction itself is the limiting factor.

annual rainfall 164.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 163.0 mm) vs barley season ET 562.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 25.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)
feasibility_meta.score_definition: probability, over input-uncertainty x parameter draws, that at least one evaluated scenario brings the best crop to relative yield >= 0.6 (FAO class S2 or better) under a reference water allocation of 8000 m3/ha/yr per unit (a scenario condition, not an observation)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 0.0-0.0 m3/ha/yr (central 0.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 2.2 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 9.2 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.56 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.expected_effect: reduce ECe 6.5 -> 0.0 dS/m (simulated); reclamation leaching depth 0.0 m water per m soil = 0.0 m3/ha one-off (C/C0 = exp(-k r), k 1.6-2.3, FAO IDP29 80-90% removal at r=1)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 15.5 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.39 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

scenarios.name: Drip irrigation with fresh groundwater + reclamation leaching, gypsum and organic amendment
residual_risks: groundwater depletion: fossil/non-renewable aquifer abstraction (aquifer yield and licence not assessed)
secondary salinisation/sodification if leaching or drainage fails
wind erosion/dust and flash-flood erosion are not modelled
soil depth and SOC come from third-party maps with no local validation (SoilGrids deserts: low skill for SOC)

uncertainty.basis: SoilGrids 2.0 vs WoSIS measured, arid held-out sites (RMSE)
SoilGrids vs WoSIS arid RMSE; low skill in deserts
assumed; no local validation

observed: slope and elevation (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM)
climate normals and interannual rainfall (TerraClimate 2011-2020, gridded climate product)
crop/ESP/salinity tolerance tables are literature (see expert_rule)
ml_predicted: ECe and ESP (own LightGBM trained on measured WoSIS/Hassani points, conformal intervals)
pH, SOC, texture, coarse fragments, bulk density, CEC (SoilGrids 2.0, third party)
depth to bedrock (SoilGrids 2017, third party, capped 200 cm)
expert_rule: Maas-Hoffman salinity response (FAO IDP29 Table 4), ESP tolerance classes (FAO SB39), pH/SOC/coarse-fragment/texture/depth/slope response curves (assumed shapes)
relative erosion index (RUSLE-type structure)
FAO suitability class boundaries on relative yield (S1>=0.8, S2 0.6-0.8, S3 0.4-0.6 [assumed], N<0.4)
simulated: intervention outcomes (leaching, gypsum, organic amendment, terracing, water harvesting)
post-restoration relative yield, class and water requirement
feasibility score and interval (Monte-Carlo)

interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

scenarios.name: Drip irrigation with fresh groundwater + reclamation leaching, gypsum and organic amendment
residual_risks: groundwater depletion: fossil/non-renewable aquifer abstraction (aquifer yield and licence not assessed)
secondary salinisation/sodification if leaching or drainage fails
wind erosion/dust and flash-flood erosion are not modelled
soil depth and SOC come from third-party maps with no local validation (SoilGrids deserts: low skill for SOC)

uncertainty.basis: SoilGrids 2.0 vs WoSIS measured, arid held-out sites (RMSE)
SoilGrids vs WoSIS arid RMSE; low skill in deserts
assumed; no local validation

observed: slope and elevation (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM)
climate normals and interannual rainfall (TerraClimate 2011-2020, gridded climate product)
crop/ESP/salinity tolerance tables are literature (see expert_rule)
ml_predicted: ECe and ESP (own LightGBM trained on measured WoSIS/Hassani points, conformal intervals)
pH, SOC, texture, coarse fragments, bulk density, CEC (SoilGrids 2.0, third party)
depth to bedrock (SoilGrids 2017, third party, capped 200 cm)
expert_rule: Maas-Hoffman salinity response (FAO IDP29 Table 4), ESP tolerance classes (FAO SB39), pH/SOC/coarse-fragment/texture/depth/slope response curves (assumed shapes)
relative erosion index (RUSLE-type structure)
FAO suitability class boundaries on relative yield (S1>=0.8, S2 0.6-0.8, S3 0.4-0.6 [assumed], N<0.4)
simulated: intervention outcomes (leaching, gypsum, organic amendment, terracing, water harvesting)
post-restoration relative yield, class and water requirement
feasibility score and interval (Monte-Carlo)

limiting_factors.detail: Model 1 class 5: legal/environmental restriction. Restoration potential is not assessed; the restriction itself is the limiting factor.

annual rainfall 149.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 140.0 mm) vs barley season ET 570.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 22.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply
coarse fragments about 24.0 vol %

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 0.0-0.0 m3/ha/yr (central 0.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 2.3 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 10.9 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.49 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]
